observation.visible_scene: A tabletop domino/marble-run arrangement on a wooden floor. In the foreground a light-wood ramp/bridge rests on two small orange cube supports, sloping down to the right, with a pale ball sitting on its raised left end. A thin white string hangs from the underside of the ramp's left end down to a tall white rectangular block positioned in front of the left orange support. A long curve of standing white dominoes sweeps from the bottom-left edge up to the ramp and onward to the right, interspersed with already-collapsed piles of purple, teal and white dominoes, plus scattered flat tiles on the floor. The background holds more upright and toppled domino patterns and wooden tower structures. The camera viewpoint is fixed across all frames.
visible_changes: The white block suspended by the string beneath the ramp's left end is initially upright and gradually tilts, swings, and finally comes to rest lying flat on the floor at the base of the white domino curve; the string attached to its top becomes visibly taut/straight during the swing before the block settles.
The pale ball remains parked on the left (high) end of the wooden ramp throughout; its position relative to the ramp does not change.

The wooden ramp, its orange supports, the far-left standing white blocks, the standing white domino curve, and all the collapsed purple/teal/white piles keep the same positions and shapes from first to last frame (no further collapse or movement is seen in this segment).
Background scenery and the overall camera framing stay constant, indicating no camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: What initiated the swing of the hanging white block (e.g., an earlier domino impact or release) is not shown within this excerpt.
Whether the ball will later roll down the ramp, and whether the block's fall triggers any further domino reaction, are not visible here.
The state of the scene before t=0 and after the last frame is unknown.
uncertain_details: It is unclear whether the swinging white block physically contacts or displaces the nearby standing white dominoes at the bottom of the curve, or merely falls beside them.
The exact attachment point and nature of the thin line (string vs. wire) is not fully resolvable.
The block's motion reads as a slow tilt accelerating into a fall, but the precise cause of the acceleration cannot be confirmed from the frames alone.
